name: ai-compiler-workbench
displayName: AI Compiler Workbench -- Agentic Graph Visualiser
description: Turns a Hugging Face causal language model into nntrainer C++ with the Claude Code CLI, verifies it against Hugging Face, and runs and profiles it in Docker.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: The workbench runs Python, the Claude CLI, compilers and Docker for the opened folder, so it only runs in a trusted workspace.

aiCompilerWorkbench.pythonPath.markdownDescription: Python interpreter for the workbench. **Leave empty** (recommended): the workbench creates and uses its own virtual environment (see `venvPath`) from a Python 3.10+ it finds on this machine, and installs torch/transformers into it on first use. Set a path only to use an existing environment (e.g. a conda env).

aiCompilerWorkbench.venvPath.markdownDescription: Where the workbench's own Python environment lives (about 1 GB). Empty = `%LOCALAPPDATA%\ai-compiler-workbench\venv` on Windows, `~/.local/share/ai-compiler-workbench/venv` elsewhere. Keep it short on Windows (torch's header paths are long).

aiCompilerWorkbench.anthropicApiKey.markdownDeprecationMessage: The API key is now kept in VS Code's secret storage: use **AI Compiler Workbench: Set Anthropic API Key**. A key still set here is moved there once and this setting is cleared.
aiCompilerWorkbench.anthropicApiKey.markdownDescription: Not used any more: run **AI Compiler Workbench: Set Anthropic API Key** instead.

aiCompilerWorkbench.claudeCliTimeout.markdownDescription: Timeout in seconds for one Claude Code CLI call. C++ generation sends a large prompt (the plan, verified code, layer catalogue, Hugging Face reference code), so the default is 900 seconds.

aiCompilerWorkbench.useClaudeCodegen.markdownDescription: Generate the nntrainer CausalLM C++ with the **Claude Code CLI**, using the local code bank (verified code from `Applications/CausalLM` is copied as is; only new parts are written). Output goes to `tools/agentic-ai-workbench/generated/<model>/`; review new parts in the **Review** tab.

aiCompilerWorkbench.claudePath.markdownDescription: Path to the `claude` executable. Leave empty to use `claude` on PATH, the native installer's `~/.local/bin/claude`, or the copy bundled with the Claude Code extension for VS Code. Sign in once by running `claude`.

aiCompilerWorkbench.claudeModel.markdownDescription: Model the Claude CLI uses for C++ generation (`sonnet`, `opus`, or a full model name).

aiCompilerWorkbench.codegenMaxAttempts.markdownDescription: How many times generated code is sent back to Claude with the checker's errors before the result is shown for review anyway.

aiCompilerWorkbench.cxxCompiler.markdownDescription: C++ compiler for the **Compile** check of generated code (it compiles the generated sources in syntax-only mode against the nntrainer checkout's headers; with an nntrainer build present it uses that build's `compile_commands.json` flags). Empty = `clang++`, `g++` or `c++` on PATH (LLVM's default folder on Windows), else MSVC (`cl` on PATH, or any Visual Studio / Build Tools install found with vswhere).

aiCompilerWorkbench.buildHost.markdownDescription: Where generated models are compile-checked and built for **Verify** (**Run** always uses Docker): `docker` = an Ubuntu 24.04 container (gcc-13, like upstream's CI) that builds a private copy of the checkout kept in a Docker volume (the checkout itself is never mounted or changed); `native` = this machine (MSVC on Windows) into `tools/agentic-ai-workbench/nb`; `auto` = Docker when it is running and its build is set up, else the native build. Docker builds are x86-64 only for now.

aiCompilerWorkbench.runMaxNewTokens.markdownDescription: **Run**: tokens the model generates after the prompt.

aiCompilerWorkbench.runRepeats.markdownDescription: **Run**: how many times the model is run; the profile shows the average.

aiCompilerWorkbench.runCpus.markdownDescription: **Run**: limit the container to this many CPUs (e.g. `2`) to imitate a smaller device. Empty = all.

aiCompilerWorkbench.runMemory.markdownDescription: **Run**: limit the container's memory (e.g. `4g`) to imitate a smaller device. Empty = no limit.

aiCompilerWorkbench.autoVerify.markdownDescription: After a passing compile check, build the generated model and run it against a tiny Hugging Face copy of the architecture (fp32 logits within 0.01 + the greedy tokens). A pass marks the approved code **verified** in the code bank, so other models reuse it. Needs **Set Up nntrainer Build** once.

aiCompilerWorkbench.autoProfile.markdownDescription: After **Verify** passes, the pipeline builds, loads and runs the generated model with its **real weights** in Docker and profiles it (tokens/s, peak memory, load time), like **Build, Run & Profile** in the Review tab. Uses **Run** settings `runMaxNewTokens`, `runRepeats`, `runCpus`, `runMemory`. Skipped, with the reason in the log, when Docker is not running, the weights are not on this computer or the model does not fit Docker's memory. The first run of a model takes a few minutes (weight conversion, runner build).

aiCompilerWorkbench.autoProfilePerLayer.markdownDescription: With **autoProfile**: after the measured runs, run the model once more against a second nntrainer build with its profiler on, for the **time of every layer**, the prompt apart from the generated tokens. The Profiler panel shows the slowest layers and opens the full table and the decoder-block map. The speeds still come from the normal build. The first time, Docker sets up the profiling build (about as long as the first build).

aiCompilerWorkbench.outputDirectory.markdownDescription: Where pipeline output goes. Empty = `tools/agentic-ai-workbench/workbench_output` of the nntrainer checkout (found from `nntrainerRepoPath`, the open folder, or the extension's own location).

aiCompilerWorkbench.nntrainerPath.markdownDescription: Path to a local nntrainer install **prefix** (a directory containing `include/nntrainer` and `lib/`), built from [nntrainer/nntrainer](https://github.com/nntrainer/nntrainer) via `meson --prefix=<this path> build && ninja -C build install`. Required only for **Profile On-Device**; everything else works without it. If left blank, the extension will use the workspace root as the nntrainer repo path.

aiCompilerWorkbench.nntrainerRepoPath.markdownDescription: Path to a local clone (via `git clone`, not a downloaded zip -- submodules require real git metadata) of the [nntrainer/nntrainer](https://github.com/nntrainer/nntrainer) source repo. Used by **Build nntrainer From Source**; defaults to workspace root if not set.

aiCompilerWorkbench.causallmProjectRoot.markdownDescription: Path to your CausalLM integration project (the one with `transformer.h`, `causal_lm.h`, `<arch>_causallm.h`), used only when **Install Generated Files** is enabled below. Generated CausalLM components (`generated_<arch>_causallm.{h,cpp}`) always get written to `<output>/generated/causallm/<arch>/` regardless of this setting -- this only controls whether they're *also* copied into your real project. Defaults to `<workspace>/Applications/CausalLM` if not set.

aiCompilerWorkbench.generatedHeaderDirec.description: Directory (relative to causallmProjectRoot) that generated .h files are copied into, when installGeneratedFiles is enabled.

aiCompilerWorkbench.generatedSourceDirec.description: Directory (relative to causallmProjectRoot) that generated .cpp files are copied into, when installGeneratedFiles is enabled.

aiCompilerWorkbench.installGeneratedFile.markdownDescription: When enabled, copies generated CausalLM `.h`/`.cpp` files into `causallmProjectRoot`'s generated-header/source directories after each run. **Off by default** -- this writes into a project outside the extension's own output directory, so it's opt-in rather than something a first run does silently.

aiCompilerWorkbench.causallmPath.markdownDescription: Path to the CausalLM repository (`Applications/CausalLM`). Required for generating `.bin` weight files. If left blank, the extension will search in common locations.
